Khurshid A lam Khan with Shahanara Begum and Md Aziz Taufique, Advocates ----- For the Petitioner. 
None appears ----- For the Respondents.
parties:
Esrarul Huq Chowdhury-----Petitioner
Vs.
Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh and others -----Respondents
full_judgment:
Md Rezaul Hasan J: In this application, filed under Article 102 (2)(a)(i) and (ii) of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, a Rule Nisi has been issued, calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the order dated 17-5-2003 passed by the respondent No. 6 in pursuance of the order dated 19-2-2003 passed by the respondent No.5 and the Memo No. 5/94/3102/1 dated 18-12-2002 of the respondent No. 3 and the Secret-Enquiry dated 16-7-2002 held at the instance of respondent Nos. 4-7 in making entry of possession of respondent No.9 in DP Khatian No. 1124. (Annexures-E, El, E2 and E3 respectively) should not be declared to have been made without any lawful authority and is of no legal effect and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. It has been stated in the writ petition, amongst other, that the petitioner is a law abiding citizen of Bangladesh; that CS khatian No. 611 of Ramnagarmouza under Dagan bhuiyan PS was prepared in the name of Badsha Mia, Lal Mia and Ershadulla alias Esadulla in respect of 53 decimal of land in plot No. 2807 and 65 decimal of land in plot No. 2810 in total 118 decimal of land; that Amirer Nessa Chowdhurani, petitioner's grandmother orally in 1921 exchanged her 107 decimal of land in plot Nos. 2699, 2702,2703 and 2705 of CS khatian No. 329 with 118 decimal of land in plot Nos. 2807 and 2810 belonged to Badsha Mia and others and she died in 1924 leaving 5 sons namely, Azizul Huq Chowdhury, Nurul-Huq Chowdhury, Hamidul Huq Chowdhury, Obaidul Huq Chowdhury and Shamsul Huq Chowdhury and they filed Partition Suit No. 1366 of 1926 and on 19-9-1927 obtained decree on solenama and Azizul Huq Chowdhury along with four brothers including the predecessor of the petitioner Obaidul Huq Chowdhury got 88 decimal of land and Shamsul Huq Chowdhury got 30 decimal of land which correctly recorded in SA khatian No. 629. On the other hand, SA khatian Nos. 333 and 334 were prepared in respect of plot Nos. 2699, 2702, 2703 and 2705 in the names of the heirs of Badsha Mia, Lal Mia and Esadulla; that Nurul Huq Chowdhury one of the SA recorded tenant died leaving 3 sons and Obaidul Huq another tenant died leaving 5 sons, one daughter including the petitioner who inherited 88 decimal out of 118 decimal of land of plot Nos. 2807 and 2810 with Hamidul Huq Chowdhury on the basis of the partition decree in Suit No. 1366 of 1926 and while in possession the BS (DP) khatian No. 1124 showing plot No. 5310 for 42 decimal 5310/5458 for 46 decimal along with other lands have been rightly prepared in the names of the petitioner along with his co-sharers and predecessor-in- interest and 30 decimal out of 118 decimal have been recorded in BS (DP) khatian No. 1138 in the names of the heirs of Shamsul Huq Chowdhury and in this way the petitioner along with his co- sharers have been possessing the entire 118 decimal of land by paying rent upto 1411 BS; that although the petitioner along with his co-sharers have been owning and possessing the 118 decimal of land with other lands since long 80 years, one Anisur Rahman Chowdhury claiming ownership of 35 decimal of land filed objection Case No. 650 under Rule 31 of the East Bengal Tenancy Rules, 1955 against the khatian prevailing in the name of the petitioner and his co-sharers and the said objection case was heard analogously with objection case No. 651 filed by said Anisur Rahman Chowdhury and both objection case No. 650 and 651 were rejected on 24-11-1997 for want of the applicant's title and possession against which said Anisur Rahman filed Appeal No. 2656 of 1998 under Rule 31 and simultaneously filed Appeal No. 2655 of 1998 against BS (DP) khatian No. 1138 in the names of the heirs of Shamsul Huq Chowdhury and both the appeals were dismissed by the judgment and order dated 14-10-2001 and the appellate authority observed that-আপীলকারী পক্ষ ১৯৪২ সনের একটি দলিল মূলে নালিশী সাবেক ২৮০৭ এবং ২৮১০ দাগের ১১৮ শতক মধ্যে ৩৫ শতক ভূমি দাবী করেন। আপীলকারী পক্ষের উক্ত দলিলের দাতাগণের নাম বা দাতাগণের মাতার নাম সি,এস রেকর্ডে নাই এবং এস,এ,রেকর্ডেও নাই। ১৯৪২ সনের দলিল মূলে জমিদারী সেরেস্তায় কোন নাম জারী হয় নাই। SA & T Act 1950 এর 19(2) ধারা অনুযায়ী আপীলকারী পক্ষ এস,এ রেকর্ড সংশোধনের ব্যবস্থা গ্রহণ করেন নাই। উক্ত Act এর 143(A) ধারার সুযোগও আপীলকারী পক্ষ গ্রহণ করেন নাই। আপীলকারী পক্ষ দেওয়ানী আদালতে কোন স্বত্ব মোকদ্দমা করেন নাই। and the appellate authority further affirmed the findings of the objection officer which was observed as “উভয় আপত্তি কেসের পক্ষগণের বক্তব্য, কাগজপত্র, সার্ভেয়ার ও উপসহকারী সেটেলমেন্ট অফিসারের তদন্ত রিপোর্ট ইত্যাদি পর্যালোচনাক্রমে দেখা যায় বাদীপক্ষ ২১-২-৮২ তারিখের ৬১২ নং দলিল মূলে সি এস রেকর্ড বহির্ভূত মালিক হইতে খরিদ করেন। কিন্তু SA  রেকর্ড করাইতে পারেন নাই এবং রেকর্ড সংশোধনের পদক্ষেপ নেন নাই। তাছাড়া সার্ভেয়ার, সাব এস,এস, ও-এর তদন্ত রিপোর্টে বাদীপক্ষেও দখল আছে মর্মে সুষ্পষ্ট রিপোর্ট পাওয়া যায় নাই। অন্যদিকে বিবাদীপক্ষ CS এবং SA রেকর্ড এবং মাননীয় মুনসেফী আদালত ফেনীর TS No.1366/1926 এর আদেশ মোতাবেক বিবাদীপক্ষেও নাম সঠিকভাবে প্রস্তুত হইয়াছে মনে করি।” that it is stated that the petitioner along- with other co-sharers filed objection case No. 235 for correction of sketch Map which was rejected against which appeal No. 5211 of 2001 under Rule 31 of the East Bengal Tenancy Rules, 1955 was preferred before the respondent No. 5 who transferred the appeal to the Assistant Settlement Officer empowered with the power of Revenue Officer and Assistant Settlement Officer, Begumganj Thana who disposed 4 appeals by the order dated 13-5-2002 directing the Surveyor to hold local investigation and to submit report to that effect; that on 3-6-2002 the appellate author- ity took up the appeal for hearing and examined the Badar investigation report which was made a part of the Judgment as the parties did not express discenting view and the appellate authority by the order dated 3-6-2002 allowed the appeal with correction of Sketch Map as prayed for in holding that “সাবেক ২৮০৭ ও ২৮১০ দাগের হাল ৫৩১০ দাগ এরিয়া ১.১৮ একরের তদন্ত রিপোর্টে দেখা যায় আপীলকারীপক্ষ উক্ত দাগের উত্তরাংশে ৪২ ডিং সর্ব দক্ষিণাংশে ৪৬ ডিং এবং প্রতিবাদীপক্ষ মধ্যাংশে ৩০ ডিং দখল করিতেছে। যাহা শুনানীকালে পক্ষ স্বীকার করেন।..................উভয়পক্ষের স্বীকৃত মতে সাবএ,এস,ও কর্তৃক প্রস্তুতকৃত বদর প্রতিবেদন মোতাবেক আপীলকারীপক্ষের দাবী মঞ্জুরক্রমে বিরোধীয় হাল ৫৩১০ দাগের ৪২ ডিং ও ৫৩১০/৫৪৫৮ দাগের ৪৬ ডিং একুনে ৮৮ ডিং ডিপি ১১৩৮ নং খতিয়ানে বহাল রহিয়া এবং প্রতিবাদী হাল দাগ ৫৩১০/৫৪৫৮ দাগ এরিয়া ৩০ শতক বহাল রাখিয়া প্রতিবাদীর ডিপি ১১৩৮  খতিয়ানে রেকর্ড করিয়া আনুষঙ্গিক সংশোধন করা হয় এবং বদর ফি বাজেয়াপ্ত করা হইল।" that it is stated that after dismissal of appeal Nos. 2656 of 1998 and 2655 of 1998 on 14-10-2001 by the order passed by Assistant Settlement Officer, Land Record and Survey Directorate, Tejgaon, Dhaka, the record of rights remained in the names of the petitioner and his co-sharers on the basis of earlier SA khatian and they have been possessing peacefully with the knowledge of all including the respondent No.9 since their predecessor-in-interest and the Judgment of the Appeal Nos. 2656 and 2655 of 1998 remained in force on the Appellant of those Appeals did not proceed to the higher forum as per provision of section 147 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act rather recently the respondent No.9 accompanied with some persons tried to disturb the possession of the petitioner and while the petitioner raised objection the respondent No. 9 claimed possession as per note in the remark column of BS (DP) khatian No. 11 24 in such way হাল ৫৩১০/৫৪৫৮ দাগে দক্ষিণঅংশেখরিদ সূত্রে ভোগদখল ২৮ র্ডিং ১৩৯৮ বাংলা সন হইতে আনিছুর রহমান চৌধুরী পিং আরিফুর রহমান চৌধুরী" which will be evident from Annexure-C to this writ petition; that it is stated that on the basis of claim of the respondent No.9 the Petitioner upon further query came to know about the order dated 17-5-2003 of the respondent No.6 in pursuance of the order dated 19-2-2003 of the respondent No.5, the Memo No. 5/94/3 102/1 dated 18-12-2002 of the respondent No.3 and the 'Secret Enquiry Report' dated 16-7- 2002 held at the instance of the respondent Nos. 4-7 by which the note regarding possession of the respondent No. 9 in the Remark Column of BS (DP) khatian No. 1124 was made although the said khatian remained in the names of the petitioner and his co-sharers; that the Revenue Appellate Authority on 14-10-2001 dismissed the appeal and settled the record of rights in the names of the petitioner and his co-sharers and in disposing the Appeal No. 5211 of 2001 for correction of Sketch Map on 3-6-2002 on the basis of Badar Report dated 22-5-2002 found possession of petitioner and his co-sharers over 42 decimal in Northern portion and 48 decimal in Southern portion of plot No. 5310 but the respondent No. 9 beyond the knowledge of the petitioner arranged a 'Secret Inquiry Report and in collusion with respondent Nos. 3, 4-7 and 9 succeeded to make entry of possession with comment that he has been possessing 28 decimal since 1398 BS which correspondence to 1991 AD but in 1997 in con testing objection cases under Rule 30 and Appeals under Rule 31 of the East Bengal Tenancy Rules, 1955 the respondent No. 9 Anisur Rahman Chowdhury did not raise that by purchase he has been possessing 28 decimal of land since 1991 AD the respondent Nos. 3, 4-7 and 9 collectively acted illegally and without lawful authority held Secret Inquiry, amended the DP khatian No. 1124 by inserting the possession of respondent No.9 in the Remark Column which is of no legal effect; that the respondent No. 4 in holding a Secret Inquiry in collusion with respondent Nos. 5-7 violated the principle of Natural Justice and also infringed the fundamental rights of the petitioner as guaranteed under Articles 27, 31 of the Constitution, as such, the act done by the respondent Nos. 3, 4, 5 and 6 are liable to be declared without lawful authority and is of no legal effect; that under Rule 31 of the Tenancy Rules, the respondent No.8 dismissed the Appeal Case No. 2655/98 and 2656/98 holding the possession of the petitioner and his co-sharers over 88 decimal as per decree dated 19-9-1927 in Partition Suit No. 1366 of 1926 and further the respondent No. 7 found possession of the petitioner and his co- sharers over 88 decimal of plot No. 5310 in holding Local Investigation in Appeal Case No. 5211 of 2001, but unfortunately the respondent No.7 was present while the respondent No. 4 held Secret Inquiry illegally and the said respondent No.7 abated the biased act of the respondent No. 4 divulging the criminal intention and misused the power and liability of a Public Officer in from of making wrong entry of another person without legal basis in the Record of Right of a law abiding citizen and this petitioner prays before your lordships to take into account such types of misconduct of a Public Officer in handling the right of citizens over their properties as conferred under Article 42(1) of the constitution as those are without lawful authority and is of no legal effect; that as soon as the petitioner came to know about the impugned orders served a notice demanding notice through his lawyer but yet received no reply or any positive act in rescinding the impugned orders; that that the petitioner was not aware of the acts done by the respondents through impugned Memo and orders and when came to know about the said orders, the period of limitation as provided under section 148 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act has already been expired and the petitioner was no other efficacious alternative forum, but to file this writ petition. 

 4. Learned Advocate Mr Khurshid Alam Khan appearing for the petitioner, first of all, submits that he has been instructed by the learned Advocates Mrs. Shahanara Begum and Mr Md Aziz Taufique to conduct hearing of this matter as a senior friend. He has next drawn our attention to an order dated 13.9.2001 and to paragraph No. 17 of the said order (Annexure- D1) and submits that said order was signed on 14-10-2001, by the Assistant Settlement Officer, who has disposed of 2 appeals, i.e. Appeal No. 2655 of 1998, against which Objection Case No. 651 dated 24-4-1997 and another Appeal No. 2656 of 1998, against which Objection Case No. 650 dated 24-11-2097, were filed. He next submits that, both Objection Miscellaneous Cases were filed under Rule 31 of the East Bengal Tenancy Rules, 1955 and the said two objection cases having been decided against the petitioner-appellants, they have preferred the aforesaid two appeals under Rule 31 of the East Bengal Tenancy Rules, 1955. He further submits that the aforesaid two appeals, being No. 2655 of 1998 and 2656 of 1998, both under Rule 31 of the East Bengal Tenancy Rules, 1955, were decided against the appellants, vide the judgment and order dated 14.10.2001, which is well reasoned and all the relevant facts have been detailed in the said judgment as well as the decision of the superior court has been referred to by the appellate authority. Besides cases of both the sides, the appellants and the respondents, has also been stated and discussed in the judgments preferred under Rule 31 of the East Bengal Tenancy Rules, 1955. The learned Advocate next submits that it has been recorded in the said judgment (Annexure- D 1) that the appellants side under Rule 31 (respondent No. 9 in this matter) has purchased the suit land by a Kabala deed No. 612 dated 21- 12-42 from the person who is not CS recorded owner and could not get their name recorded in SA Khatian. The appellate authority, under Rule 31, has further recorded in his judgment that the CS and SA record were prepared in the name of the respondents i.e. the writ petitioners in this matter, pursuant to judgment passed by the then Munsif Court, Feni, in Title Suit No. 1366 of 1926 and that the writ petitioner is representing the interest of other writ petitioners (respondents in appeal filed under Rule 31) as one of the family members. He also submits that after bare elaborate discussion of the facts and circumstances of the case of the parties and narrating facts as well as the circumstances of the case of both the sides and then having considered all material facts and documents along with the decisions of the higher court and the concerned law, the aforesaid judgment were passed in Appeal Nos. 2655 of 1998 and 2656 of 1998, both filed under Rule 31 of the East Bengal Tenancy Rules, 1955 and were heard and disposed of analogously, whereby both the appeals were disallowed. In this situation and in the light of the background, facts and circumstances of this case, the learned Advocate emphatically submits, that the impugned orders dated 17- 5-2003, 19-2-2003,18-12-2002 and the impugned secret enquiry dated 16-7-2002 and making entry of possession in the name of the respondent No.9, Anisur Rahman Chowdhury, Son of Late Alhaj Arifur Rahman Chowdhury, who was one of the appellants in the column NO.9 of the concerned Kabuliat, as possessors is totally without jurisdiction, ultra vires and is of no legal effect and all the impugned orders along with said direction is liable to be struck down. In support of his contention challenging the impugned orders, the learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that, after final disposal of the aforesaid 2 appeals filed under Rule 31 of the East Bengal Tenancy Rules, 1955, the respondent No.3 had no authority or jurisdiction, what so ever, to entertain any application filed by Anisur Rahman Chowdhury and others or to pass the impugned orders (Annexures- E, E1, E2 and E3) after the final order was passed and signed on 14-10-2001, by the appellate authority, under Rule 31 of the East Bengal Tenancy Rules, 1955 i.e. the Assistant Settlement Officer (Annexure-D 1). He also submits that in the impugned orders the respondent No.3 has admitted that he has taken up the matter ex-parte for disposal. On this point the learned Advocate asserts that, 'but it has been recorded in the impugned order that the notice has been served upon the other side. Admittedly no notice was served the matter was heard ex-parte by the respondent No. 3 and there is no materials on record to show that any notice had been served before passing the impugned order and the entire proceedings, impugned before this court as well as the impugned orders were passed behind the back of the petitioner and secretly in connivance with the respondent No. 9 (Anisur Rahman Chowdhury) and others, the learned Advocate adds. The learned Advocate further submits that, it shows malafide on the part' of the respondent No. 3. Besides, he also submits, that the impugned order passed by the respondent No.3 is not supported by any materials on record, although the impugned orders are beyond the authority inasmuch as the appellate authority has disposed of both the appeals under Rule 31 of the East Bengal Tenancy Rules, 1955. The case of the petitioner has neither been controverted nor been denied by any of the respondents by filing any affidavit-in-opposition. 

 "Once appeal has been disposed of on contest under Rule 31 of Rules, no review or other application lies and the settlement authority have got no jurisdiction to re-open the matter other than to send the draft publication khatian for final publication under Rule 32 of the Rules. Even Rule 42 does not empower the settlement Officer to sit and act as an appellate authority over an appellate order passed under Rule 31 of the Rules." 

 In the result, the Rule is made absolute. Order dated 17-5-2003 Annexures- E, E1, E2 and E3 respectively is hereby declared to have been passed without any lawful authority and is of no legal effect. In consequence thereof, the respondents are directed to delete the name of entry of respondent No.9, Anisur Rahman Chowdhury, Son of Late Al-haj Arifur Rahman Chowdhury, as possessor, from the concerned column of the concerned Khatian, within 30 days on receiving this judgment and order.
